icon.description: Slot: ReactNode. No JSON Schema type exists for it; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.slots.

render.description: TS: import("@types/react/index").ReactElement<unknown, string | import("@types/react/index").JSXElementConstructor<any>> | import("@base-ui/react/types/index").ComponentRenderFn<import("@base-ui/react/types/index").HTMLProps, import("@base-ui/react/button/Button").ButtonState> | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc.

style.description: TS: import("@types/react/index").CSSProperties | ((state: import("@base-ui/react/button/Button").ButtonState) => import("@types/react/index").CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc.

x-uikit.intent: Trigger a single action in the current context.
typical_uses: A one-off action with an immediate effect (submit, confirm, open a dialog)
An icon-only action that has an accessible name (pass aria-label)

invariants.text: With `icon` set and no children the button renders icon-only and carries no accessible name of its own - `aria-label` is required.

While `loading`, the button stays in the tab order and reports `aria-disabled`/`aria-busy`; it never becomes natively `disabled`, so `:disabled` selectors and the `disabled` DOM property do not see it.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a spinner next to the label by hand
anti_patterns.instead: Use `loading` - it preserves the button's width and accessible name

anti_patterns.dont: Pass an icon element through children

good.title: Variant and size on a plain action

bad.title: Icon passed through children
bad.why: Children are text only. An icon in children misses the slot that sizes it, spaces it, hides it while `loading` and marks it `aria-hidden`, so it is announced as part of the accessible name.

bad.title: Spinner rendered by hand
bad.why: `loading` exists for this: it keeps the button's width, keeps the accessible name and reports `aria-busy` while staying focusable. A native `disabled` blurs the button the instant it lands, so the busy state is announced to nobody.

instead.external: the consumer app's link component (a plain anchor when the app has none)
instead.note: This kit ships no Link component, and no kit component is a substitute for one: navigation belongs to the app's own router. An action that must read as a button while it navigates stays on Button, rendered over a real anchor - `render={<a href="..." />}` with `nativeButton={false}`.

assumptions.claim: icon is a React node, not a value
assumptions.reason: `ReactNode` has no JSON Schema representation - an element, a string, a fragment and `false` are all valid and only tsc can tell them from a mistake. The slot exists so the icon gets sized, spaced, hidden while `loading` and marked decorative; what may go in it is "anything React renders", which is the whole assertion.

assumptions.claim: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
assumptions.reason: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema. It is what makes `render={<a href="..." />}` with `nativeButton={false}` the way to keep an action reading as a button while it navigates.

assumptions.claim: style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object
assumptions.reason: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state. A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through `variant`/`size` and CSS Modules, not through this.
